sources.entry: lightgbm - A fast, distributed, high-performance gradient boosting framework.

summary.one_liner: LightGBM is a fast, distributed, high-performance gradient boosting framework based on tree-learning algorithms, maintained at the lightgbm-org/LightGBM repository (moved from Microsoft/LightGBM in March 2026).
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LightGBM as a gradient boosting framework using tree-based learning algorithms, aimed at fast training, lower memory use, and good accuracy. It states support for parallel, distributed, and GPU learning, and says it is meant to handle large-scale data. It points to external documentation for installation, examples, features, and a full parameter list. It also lists tuning integrations (FLAML, Optuna) and a long set of unofficial projects that offer alternative ways to use LightGBM, such as model compilers, inference libraries, language bindings, and time-series extensions. The README includes reference papers on the underlying algorithms and is released under the MIT license.
use_cases: train gradient boosted decision trees on tabular data
how_to_run: Follow the installation instructions on the official documentation site (linked from the README, not included in it)
notable: Supports parallel, distributed, and GPU learning
Lower memory usage and faster training than other boosting frameworks, per the README's comparison claims
Large ecosystem of unofficial integrations for serving, explaining, and converting models
Official changelogs are kept on the GitHub releases page
Based on published papers including quantized training of GBDTs (NeurIPS 2022)
caveats: Installation and usage details are on an external documentation site rather than in the README
Listed external projects are not maintained or endorsed by the LightGBM team
Repository moved from Microsoft/LightGBM to lightgbm-org/LightGBM in March 2026, so older links may point to the former location
